definition: Connecting a model's output to real, verifiable sources or data instead of letting it answer from memory alone.
details: Grounded systems retrieve documents or query tools, then constrain the answer to what those sources support — which reduces hallucination and makes claims auditable. Retrieval-augmented generation is the most common way to implement it.
story: Think of a jazz musician who has heard so many solos that a new one simply falls out of their fingers. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. It makes new things by recombining everything it has ever seen. Creation, here, is memory recombined at speed. That next-word, next-stroke magic is Grounding.

citation.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (NeurIPS)
